headNote:
CARRIED FORWARD FROM `main` WITH THIS BRANCH'S THREE ADDITIONS, on the convergence onto `main` at `3afcc732f` (PR #290's user-card measure, itself folded on `ced025203`, PR #248's band-occlusion fold - `main` moved twice while this round's reviews ran). WHY THIS FILE IS NOW MAIN'S RATHER THAN THIS BRANCH'S: the branch's own manifest chain was written against a base a hundred commits old, and every field in it that is DERIVED - the stamps, the swept count, the surface count, `partialCapture` - describes the tree it was written ON. The rebase moved both trees again, so carrying the branch's values forward would have shipped numbers for a tree that no longer exists. WHAT THIS BRANCH OWNS IS THREE ADDITIONS AND NOTHING ELSE, spliced verbatim into main's file: its declared supplementary set (`composer-status-clear`, 18 surfaces in both brand palettes), its `roundThreeLeftoversPass` record inside `remediationRecord`, and its `captureOrigin.browserToolPass` note. Everything else here is upstream's, `captureOrigin.reStamps` included. THE STAMPS are read from the tree this commit ships - `git rev-parse HEAD:src` / `HEAD:scripts` - and `frames` (4,966) is the swept count on disk outside every declared supplementary set while `surfaces` (552) is the story list `scripts/capture-evidence.mjs` declares, both re-derived here rather than carried, which is what `countsMean` and the stamps exist to force. `head` names the commit this lineage carries the branch's work in, which is the commit BEFORE the stamp block, because a stamp cannot cite the commit that contains it. The four frames this round re-shot differ from the ones this branch carried in one caption line each and nowhere else, measured against the decoded previous frames: 952x23px at `583,56` for the long-goal story's caption and 2001x25px at `54,968` for the in-flight harness band's, identical in both palettes. D9, THE BAND'S GEOMETRY: the full-bleed bands are the shell's first children in flow, so the region below them is the window minus their height and no row can be covered at any band height. RE-STAMPED FOR THE REBASE ONTO `main`'s `efa8b2fab` (PR #263, the machine panels without a session), WHICH MOVED BOTH TREES UNDER THIS BRANCH: `src/` in 22 files and `scripts/` in 11, so `srcTree` and `scriptsTree` are re-derived here from the tree that ships rather than carried from either side of the rebase - and the conflict WAS in this file's head block, where taking a side ships one of the two stale pairs and drops the other's re-stamp commit, which is the failure the previous re-stamp in this field records. WHAT MOVED: `src/` - five files under `src/renderer/src` (the shell root becomes a flex column with the two bands as its first children, the region becomes `flex-1 min-h-0`, and both band wrappers drop `fixed inset-x-0 top-0` with the z-index that existed only to clear chrome they covered), and the comments in the palette and the dialog that justified their stacking level by citing that spelling. `scripts/` - the band rig (`scripts/band-occlusion-evidence.mjs`) and one invariant in `scripts/palette-contract.test.mjs`, which now asserts the shape a revert would break, plus the spawn-site table row the rig needs and the two rigs whose band readers were re-wired to the shape that exists. WHAT DID NOT MOVE: every committed `.webp`, and with them `frames`, `surfaces` and `themes`, which are this head's own arithmetic (4,930 swept, 547 `STORIES` rows, 12 themes) - re-derived by `check-evidence.mjs`'s own walker against this tree, not carried: the step from the branch's pre-rebase 4,125/504 is `main`'s own evidence work, not this branch's, whose frames are PNGs under `docs/evidence/band-occlusion/` that the sweep does not walk and are re-derived below rather than carried. WHY THE HASHES MOVE ANYWAY: `srcTree`/`scriptsTree` describe the tree the frames SHIP IN, not the tree they depict - the `before/` half is a picture of the pre-fix tree by construction, so re-capturing it does not move these stamps. `head` is the commit that carries this evidence, re-spelled for this lineage (`753fbceb0` -> `43a70840d`) because a rebase re-spells every citation; `partialCapture`'s own citations are `main`'s and are untouched by the rebase for the same reason its counts were already right. FOLDED A THIRD TIME WHILE THIS PASS RAN, onto `main`'s `ace40b3b6` (the TUI theme port and 21 more commits), and re-derived for it on the same argument as the two before: the fold's `src/` delta is 86 files - 49 added (47 palettes, plus the theme grid's own new `theme-grid-navigation.ts` and a `theme-selector.stories.tsx`), 32 comment-only, and five that change code (`settings/components/theme-selector.tsx`, `shared/themes/index.ts`, `shared/themes/palette-contract.ts`, `shared/types/theme.ts`, `styles/themes.generated.css`), none of the five on the captured `#/chat` or `#/browser` route - and that classification is a per-file comment-stripped comparison rather than a summary of the fold, taken because the summary this field carried before it (palettes and generated theme CSS) describes 48 of the 86 files - the palettes and `themes.generated.css` - and leaves the 32 comment-only files, the other four code changes and the two non-palette additions out of the account, hiding the one a design reader would want named: `shared/components/ui/alert.tsx`, the component both bands render, which is comment-only across the fold like `chat-sidebar.tsx`, `chat-content.tsx`, `message-input.tsx` and `keyboard-shortcut.tsx`. The two palettes this scene PAINTS are untouched - `localOperatorDark` is unchanged and is still `DEFAULT_THEME`, and the fold only ADDS themes (it does not move the ones the frames were taken in). So the frames remain pictures of the shell they were taken from, and the counts here are the walker's on the tree this commit ships (`frames` 4,871 -> 4,930 and `surfaces` 546 -> 547 are the fold's). `head` is re-spelled for this lineage once more: `467890d7c`, the commit that carries the pair. Note for the next author: taking a SIDE of this file's conflict during a rebase is how the re-stamp commit gets silently dropped - it happened twice in this pass, and the file survived only because it was rewritten afterwards rather than merged. FOLDED ONCE MORE, onto `main`'s `013aad424` (the transcript-timestamps and header-cluster merges), and RE-STAMPED FOR IT RATHER THAN RE-CAPTURED, which is the call this field has to justify: the fold moves twelve files under `src/` and NOT ONE of them is reachable from this scene. The scene is a sessionless `#/chat` - its own frame shows the pane's DRAFT branch (`chat-page.tsx`: no `identity`, so `Start a chat` and no transcript) - while the fold's delta is `chat-header.tsx`, `canonical-transcript.tsx`, the message and turn timestamps, `conversation-divider`, the trace rows and the date utilities, every one of which renders only inside a session that this rig never has. `app.tsx`, the two band components, `chat-page.tsx`, `chat-sidebar.tsx`, `dialog.tsx` and the command palette are BYTE-IDENTICAL across the fold, and the counts above are re-derived from the tree this commit ships. The band pair's own frames are unchanged pictures of an unchanged shell; what the fold moves is `srcTree`, and this stamp is where that belongs. RE-STAMPED ONCE MORE BY THE PAIR PASS, whose `scripts/` delta is the rig alone (`scripts/band-occlusion-evidence.mjs`, `scriptsTree` 4a81d54ac -> 33cfdc15e): the expression it sends did not parse, its pane probe read the sidebar, its pixel assertion never ran, and its `scrim` state could not be reached - four defects that made the instrument unrunnable and are named in `docs/evidence/band-occlusion/README.md`. No file under `src/` moves in that pass (the conflict resolution for the rebase landed in the fix itself), no frame is re-taken that the stamp describes, and `srcTree`, `head`, `capturedAt`, `frames`, `surfaces` and `themes` are unchanged - the band pair's own PNGs are not WebP and the sweep does not walk them. `app.tsx`'s conflict resolution for this rebase is the one part of the branch's own change that this commit's stamps had to be re-derived AROUND: the branch's column and its two bands are kept WHOLESALE and `main`'s `PanelOutlet` is re-inserted into the region above `<main>`, which is where it has to be for its mount-order invariant and where the region's `overflow-hidden` cannot clip it because it presents a Radix `Dialog` that  FOLDED ONTO `main`'s `562bc5837` (the 0.26.0 release, `package.json`; PR #295's fold-stamp notes in `AGENTS.md` and `scripts/capture-evidence.mjs`; and `main`'s own head block in this file), and RE-STAMPED FOR IT RATHER THAN RE-CAPTURED on the argument every fold before it used: no file under `src/` moves on either side and no `.webp` is added, so `frames`, `surfaces` and `themes` are unchanged and re-checked against the merged tree, and TWO causes move `scriptsTree` rather than one: `main`'s #295 edits `scripts/capture-evidence.mjs`, which is not a frame, AND this branch's own round-2 remediation commit `2f5f0fe0e` moved `scripts/` to `463c427f4c31` while its copy of this file still declared `bf3d2495a7e5` - the value true of `44b68172b` - so the pre-fold head shipped a STALE stamp of exactly the class this field exists to expose, which `scripts/evidence-manifest.test.mjs`'s shipped-manifest stamp case (line 725, present at that head too) fails with no lease, and which no CI saw because no check run exists on that commit (`check-runs` `total_count: 0`). The fold repaired both, not just #295's half. The head block was the conflict, and it is resolved per FIELD rather than by taking a side: `head` stays this branch's and `headNote` is the branch's own text kept as its BASE with this fold's paragraph APPENDED (6,599 -> 7,606 chars, and the appended paragraph is the text making this claim) - these frames were taken on `467890d7c`'s tree, and `main`'s `4cd055f87` names a different pass over the same inventory - while both stamps are re-derived here from the MERGED tree, in the commit that carries them, which is the ordering `AGENTS.md`'s fold note now states and fold 11 got wrong by deriving before the merge commit existed. RECORD CORRECTION (review round 3, F1/F2): this field first named ONE cause of the `scriptsTree` movement and said `headNote` 'stayed' this branch's; both clauses are corrected in place above, in the docs-only commit answering that round, while the fold commit and the PR's `Fold note` comment, which carry the earlier wording verbatim, are history and are not rewritten.

FOLDED ONTO `main`'s `47a7d5e37` (the 0.26.1 release, `#298`; `#207`'s run-panel reveal, which moves `src/`; and the other lanes' fold-stamp commits - 50 files, +14285/-55, with BOTH trees moved) AND RE-STAMPED FOR IT RATHER THAN RE-CAPTURED on the argument every fold before this one used: no `.webp` is added or removed by this fold, no frame is re-taken, and `frames` (4,930), `surfaces` (547) and `themes` (12) are re-checked against the merged tree rather than carried, so the frames remain pictures of the tree they ship in. IT IS A MERGE AND NOT A REBASE, so no branch commit is rewritten and `9a042035f` stays an ancestor - which is what the round SHAs in the PR thread are read against. THE HEAD BLOCK WAS THE CONFLICT, and it is resolved per FIELD rather than by taking a side: `head` stays this branch's `467890d7c` (the commit these frames came from, which `captureOrigin` also records) and `headNote` is this branch's own text kept as its BASE with this paragraph APPENDED, while BOTH STAMPS are re-derived from the MERGED tree in the commit that carries them - neither side's pair survives, this branch's being `dcff3db3f`/`fba799f56` and main's `f4165c26a`/`cdbf344e4`, because the merged tree is neither's - and the derivation happens after the merge commit exists, which is the ordering `AGENTS.md`'s fold note states and fold 11 got wrong by deriving before the merge did. The pair this fold derived is `6b8507807` for `src/` and `7abf70a2b` for `scripts/`, read from the fold commit's own trees. MAIN'S OWN VALUES, DISPLACED BY THIS FOLD AND NAMED HERE RATHER THAN DROPPED: its 2,447,070-character `headNote` (unchanged between `562bc5837` and `47a7d5e37`), its `head` `6cb1445b5`, and its stamps `f4165c26a`/`cdbf344e4`. THE FOLD CHANGES NOTHING OF THIS BRANCH'S OWN CHANGE, measured rather than asserted: `git diff --name-status 562bc5837 9a042035f` and `git diff --name-status 47a7d5e37 <this fold's head>` are the same 37 paths with the same status letters and the same totals - 26 added, 11 modified - path for path. REACHABILITY, ARGUED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, because `main` moved `src/` this time: its 11 files are all `#207`'s run pane - `chat-content.tsx`, the six `run-details/` files, `run-panel.tsx`, `pickers/panels/story-scroll.ts`, `shared/lib/scroll.ts` and `shared/store/ui-preferences-store.ts` - and none is reachable from a surface this PR alters or from the captured scene. `shared/lib/scroll.ts` is imported by `run-panel.tsx` and by the storybook-only `story-scroll.ts` and by nothing else in `src/`; `story-scroll.ts` says as much itself (`Nothing in the app imports this file`); `chat-content.tsx` does paint the captured `#/chat` pane, but every line this fold brings it lives behind `{isRunPanelOpen && runDetails}` - the two refs added to the row and the column draw nothing, and the width, divider and `paneWidth` changes are inside the run pane's own block - while the run pane is shut in all ten driven states and all five recorded anchors (`chatSearch`, `chatListHeader`, `paneFirstRow`, `railSearch`, `browserContent`) sit outside it; `ui-preferences-store.ts`'s delta is `DEFAULT_RUN_PANEL_WIDTH` gaining `export` and a docblock, a binding rather than a value; and the six `run-details/` files with `run-panel.tsx` are that same unopened pane. No upstream `src/` file reachable from this change therefore changed materially, and the fold stops for nothing. `scripts/` moved in four files (three added, one modified), which is the fold's other cause. THE REST OF THE FILE AUTO-MERGED AND COMES OUT AS THE UNION: `supplementary` 71 -> 72 (main's `run-panel-reveal` set, which claims the frames `#207` added; every set this branch declares is already in main's list), `captureOrigin` main's, which is a strict superset of this branch's (its `reStamps` entry), and `partialCapture`, `frames`, `surfaces`, `themes`, `capturedAt` and `dirtyWorkingTree` identical on both sides. CARRIED FORWARD AGAIN ON THE REBASE ONTO `main`'s `da9540148` (PR #278, the panel load latency, merged over `3afcc732f`'s user-bubble measure; `main` moved while the round-4 reviews ran, and GitHub reports this PR `DIRTY` for it, which is also why a dirty head has no CI run of its own). WHAT IS RE-DERIVED, group 4, FROM THE TREE THIS COMMIT SHIPS: `srcTree`/`scriptsTree` are `git rev-parse HEAD:src`/`HEAD:scripts`; `frames` is the swept count `check-evidence.mjs`'s own walker reads (4,966 committed WebP files outside the 74 declared sets, of 5,880 on disk) and `surfaces` is the `STORIES` list's own length (552), both taken from the merged tree rather than from either side; `themes` is 12. WHAT DID NOT MOVE: every committed `.webp`, and with them every count above, and every file outside this one - proved per commit and whole-branch by the method `remediationRecord.roundThreeLeftoversPass.rangeDiffProof` states. THE CITATIONS THIS REBASE RE-SPELLED, both re-pointed at `e81799185`, this lineage's spelling of the commit the branch's frames were shot from (`fb06ca75f` before this rebase, `4db07c5cc` and `5e2d0bffa` before that): `head` itself, and `supplementary[composer-status-clear].capturedAtHead`. `captureOrigin.browserToolPass.capturedAtHead` follows them (`fbeda5bff` -> `839ca4772`); no gate reads that field and it is re-pointed because a reader can check it. `supplementary`, `captureOrigin` and `remediationRecord` are otherwise the state the round-4 reviews passed, with the branch's three additions - the `composer-status-clear` set, its `roundThreeLeftoversPass` record and its `browserToolPass` note - spliced verbatim into main's file. `scripts/composer-tabs.test.mjs` auto-merged again, as it does in every convergence, and the merged suite is what says the two sides' additions do not overlap. ROUND 3, A RE-CAPTURE WITH THE GATE OPEN, and its re-stamps since: the `settings-backend` stories advertised `features: { settings: 1 }` and nothing else, so `auth` and `catalogues` were closed, neither op was issued, and four directories were ONE PICTURE (`catalogue-in-flight`, `catalogue-partial`, `catalogue-unknown-credentials`, `model-list-open` hashed identically in all twelve themes - design round 2, D6). With the features granted in the fixture, 264 frames on that surface and 132 on `settings-model-combobox` were re-shot, the four now have their own bytes, and `settings-backend/hosting-list-open/` was retired. Eight `settings-model-combobox/after/` frames were re-taken from the live app. ACROSS THE FIVE REBASES SINCE, both surfaces have been re-captured in full each time rather than reasoned about - every frame came back byte-identical, so no frame directory has ever collided with an arrival. WHAT THE FIELDS MEAN: `srcTree` and `scriptsTree` are re-derived from the tree that ships; `surfaces` is the STORIES table's own row count as the gate counts it; `frames` and `partialCapture.refreshedFrames` are re-derived from `docs/evidence`, because a narrowed run's arithmetic adds only what a NEW surface contributed and would otherwise carry the previous pass's total - the value this file's gate rejects by name; `head` and `partialCapture.refreshedAtHead` name the commit this lineage carries the pass in, since a rebase re-spells the commit they used to name.

WHY TWICE: the first settings run was taken before the degraded row's state word was moved off the label (as a suffix it wrapped the label column and pushed the number below its siblings' baseline, which the frame itself is what caught), and the LAST run of each surface was taken over the committed tree so the tree stamps below describe the pixels. The set this pass wrote and re-verified is 26 stories x 2 palettes = 52 frames - that is `refreshedFrames` - of which 16 surfaces x 2 palettes = 32 were NEW (`addedSurfaces`/`addedFrames`): four new states and the value's hover frame on the wide surface, a new narrow surface of three stories, and the eight-story `common-connectivity-banner` surface, which had NO frame anywhere in the tree before this pass. `refreshedFromHead` is the previous head of this branch rather than the first pass's own start, so the gate's denominator spans only the frames this pass's commits can have moved. Re-running each command reproduced every frame byte for byte at this head, which is what makes a re-take comparable rather than merely similar; the three surfaces' READMEs state the readback, the md5s and what the frames do not prove, and `common-connectivity-banner-baseline` is this pass's declared before-half. DETERMINISM, measured twice over: the first capture of the degraded row came back with a DIFFERENT hash on a second run of the same tree, and the cause was the rig rather than the component - a `{ hover }` entry moves the real pointer for its own frame and nothing moved it back, so the next story (and the next run) loaded with the pointer already inside the row's value, where a tooltip opens on a 400 ms delay. `capture-evidence.mjs` now parks the pointer at the bottom-right of the requested viewport before every navigation, and after that fix two consecutive runs of the settings surface are byte-identical 26/26 and two of the connectivity banner 16/16. The final capture of each surface was taken over the committed tree, which is why `dirtyWorkingTree` is false. What that fix does NOT claim: whether any frame outside these three surfaces was captured with a residual pointer before it; a future full sweep may produce different bytes for such a frame, and that would be the fix taking effect.

previousRefresh.note: MAIN'S OWN NARROWED PASS, carried through whole under this branch's block because it ran later than the pass this branch's block records and it is main's record, not this branch's. The narrowed runs this branch has taken on top of the last full sweep, which is what `countsMean.frames` is asserted against. FIRST, the ask-options remediation recapture, cited at `bfcc614e9` - this branch's current spelling of that commit. Its earlier spellings went unreachable each time the branch was rebased (onto v0.21.0, twice more during round 4, and again onto v0.22.1), which is the re-pointing repair the manifest's other citations carry: a citation is only evidence if a reader can resolve it. The spelling is `git range-diff`'s over the fourteen replayed commits rather than this note's positional guess, and the pairings are the ones it reports: entry 4 (`2523612b6`, the recapture this run repeated), entries 7, 8, 11, 12 and 14 carry IDENTICAL patches across the rebase, and entry 5 is the single pair whose patch differs - in exactly one file, `scripts/vite-plugins/desktop-proxy.ts`, where that commit's 22 added lines are 15 lines of comment plus the seven-line guard `if (res.headersSent) { res.destroy(); return; }`. Those seven lines are present in this lineage byte-for-byte, landed independently by `main`'s own `8505bb752`, so only the duplicate comment prose is dropped and `main`'s own comment for the same guard stands in its place. Every other file's added and removed line sets are byte-identical between the two spellings, `scripts/click-proof.mjs` (309 added lines) and this set's `harness/ask-gate.vite.mjs` (167) among them, whose blob hashes are equal. It was a `--only=chat-ask-options` run: 122 frames moved, read out of `git diff --name-status 2523612b6 -- docs/evidence` filtered to `.webp` rather than counted by hand - 86 rewritten in place (84 in the swept set and the live pair's 2), 24 added as the two width-suffixed entries above (`wrapping-labels` existed only as the single-width `chat-ask-options/wrapping-labels/` before it, which is design round 1's D5: a story id captured at two widths is written with its width in the path), and 12 stale duplicates deleted rather than left behind, because a second copy of the same story at the same 1024 column would have been stale evidence counted as swept. `check-evidence.mjs` asserts the 120 of those 122 that fall outside the declared sets, which is why `refreshedFrames` exceeds the moved `.webp` count and why the deleted 12 are in it. SECOND, this round's re-verification: the same `--only=chat-ask-options` run at `refreshedAtHead`, the narrowed run's full nine entries across all twelve themes, 108 frames - re-taken to check that the frames are still pictures of this head's `src` rather than to re-argue it, and every one of the 108 came back byte-identical to the committed frame on disk (`git status docs/evidence` after the run names this manifest and nothing else). It ran twice, at `refreshedFromHead` and again at `refreshedAtHead`, the second time once the gate and harness repairs were committed so that `dirtyWorkingTree` would describe committed source; `refreshedFrames` is 216 rather than 108 because the capturer accumulates across the runs of one pass while the head stays inside that pass's ancestry - the count is frames taken, and 216 were taken, the second 108 of them moving no bytes. It is recorded because it is what licenses the tree stamps above. `frames` and `surfaces` are re-derived from the tree and from the capturer's own list as they stand rather than incremented from the previous values, which is what the capture script's own `+ addedSurfaces.length` would have got wrong here (the two new entries share one story ID, so the entry count moved by one and the directory count by two) and wrong again on this rebase, where upstream's list grew under this branch: 152 of the 161 swept entries are `main`'s own. One more narrowed run is recorded here because this file is the manifest's only per-run record and this round would otherwise have erased it: `main`'s tool-row round (`--only=chat-tool-rows`, refreshed 26 frames across 12 stories, 0 added, at `59997deb1`), which is where `chat-tool-rows/*` and the `tool-rows-4px-rejected` set come from. `previousRefresh` above is the model-picker remediation's two runs, unchanged, because they are still true of frames on disk. `refreshedStories` names this branch's own entries and nothing else. It carried nine `canvas-workspace--*` ids when this block's citation fields still described `main`'s pass; the branch's own pass replaced those fields, and a story list for a pass the block no longer cites is a record of something else, so it is deleted rather than left to disagree with the citation beside it. `main`'s own manifest still records that pass, which is where a reader following those ids should look. THIS BRANCH'S PASS (the composer status tabs) is the fourth narrowing recorded here, and the mechanical fields above are now ITS values — which is why the sentences in the paragraph above that name `refreshedAtHead`, `refreshedFrames` and `refreshedStories` describe the ask-options pass at ITS pass start rather than this one, their citations unchanged and their own record untouched. FIRST, `--only=chat-composer-status-row --themes=localOperatorDark,localOperatorLight`: four new stories, eight frames, all eight added, and those four surfaces are the ones `addedSurfaces` names above. SECOND, `--only=chat-run-panel` at the same two palettes, for the run trigger's `Activity` to `Info` swap (`docs/composer-status-tabs.md` § 6): the WHOLE set re-taken rather than the three `trigger-*` stories, because every story in it mounts the production `ChatHeader` and refreshing three of thirty-nine would leave one directory showing two glyphs. `frames` and `surfaces` are re-derived from the tree rather than carried from that run, and the reason is the capturer's own `+ addedSurfaces.length` arithmetic: the first attempt at that re-take was narrowed to `--only=chat-run-panel--trigger` and wrote those three stories in all twelve palettes, ten of which did not exist before, so it counted three EXISTING surfaces as new and raised `surfaces` to 168 and `frames` to 1202 — and those thirty frames were then deleted, because a re-take that changes a set's declared two-brand-theme shape is a different set. The set is 39 stories over two themes — 78 frames — again. THE MUTATION IS MEASURED ON THE FRAMES WHOSE FIXTURES HOLD NO LIVE CLOCK, and the rig is deterministic, which is what makes the measurement mean anything: `trigger-idle/localOperatorLight` captured three times at one head is byte-identical all three times, so a frame's diff against its committed predecessor is its input's diff. On the six brand-theme `trigger-*` frames, four differ only inside the glyph's own 16x16 box (`15x16+381+20`, two at `16x16+380+20`, `15x16+781+20`; AE 5,311 to 21,056 pixels) and two differ over a wider box whose worst band measures a maximum of 17/255 and 16/255 at means of 0.15 and 0.21 — the header's text and rules at identical positions, i.e. the lossy encoder reallocating blocks around the one block whose content moved, where a rendering change lands at 50-250 levels on edges. The ROSTER stories are a different case, and it is not this change: they photograph a running child's live clock. `roster-members/localOperatorDark` captured twice at one head differs by 5,560 pixels (0.62% of the frame) confined to a `15x56+1171+82` strip — the elapsed-time and percentage digits of two rows, `19s`/`2m31s` against `18s`/`2m30s`. That is content rather than sheen, and the ask-options paragraph above reads the same magnitude as anti-aliasing; the mechanism is the clock, which is also why 35 of the 78 frames moved again on this rebase's re-capture while all eight of the composer row's came back byte-identical. `docs/evidence/chat-run-details/` was NOT re-taken and cannot be: it is a declared preserved record of the retired popover whose story ids are gone from `STORIES`, which is what its own `supplementary` entry says — so the design record's § 9.2 sentence naming it as a story set this change re-takes is stale on that point. Its twenty frames still show the old glyph, and they are a record of a surface the tree no longer has rather than evidence about the one it does.

imageExpandPass.what: This branch's own evidence: the conversation picture expanded over the app, three stories over twelve themes.

imageExpandPass.runs: TWO runs. The first photographed a 960x600 fixture, which is smaller than the 90vw/90vh box the overlay offers a picture, so `expanded` showed the natural-size path and the fit-to-viewport path was never exercised. imageExpandPass.fixtureAspectConstraint: The `expanded` fixture is WIDER than the viewport (1600x600) because `check-evidence`'s ground check requires a frame's dominant colour to sit within ΔE00 25 of one of the theme's four grounds: a picture fitted to 1280x900 with a near-square aspect fills most of the frame, so its own white becomes the dominant colour - measured, a 1200x750 fixture at this viewport failed at ΔE00 79.41 from the nearest `localOperatorDark` ground, the same number the check's header records for the blank frame it was written for.
imageExpandPass.measured: Off the committed frames, by thresholding the picture's light ground and trimming to it: `expanded` is 1152x432 at +64,+234 in a 1280x900 frame (the 90vw cap binding, 64px on each side = the 5% margin), and `expanded-small-image` is 240x180 at +200,+120 in a 640x420 frame - the picture's own size, in a box of 576x378 it never used.
imageExpandPass.dirtyWorkingTree: TRUE, and the dirt is named: at capture time this branch's edit to `scripts/capture-evidence.mjs` (the three declared story rows) was in the working tree and not yet committed, so the tree hash written here is of the commit the frames were painted from rather than of the working tree. The story file was committed and then edited once more (the wider fixture), which is why this file ends with a re-stamp commit after the story and rig commits land.
imageExpandPass.notCovered: A real-engine pointer press aimed at a POINT outside the picture. The `browser` tool clicks an element by selector and cannot aim at a coordinate, and this surface's centre IS the picture; the scrim press is evidenced by the element the press lands on (jsdom) plus the measured geometry that makes that element genuinely outside the layer. A coordinate-capable harness closes it - QA's place, named in the set's README rather than implied away.

previousPartialCapture.provenanceNote:
THE REBASE, and the first one here that re-stamps without re-capturing. `main` moved three times under this branch during the round - to `e4d074c60` (0.19.6), to `98c32e85e` (0.19.7 plus #138, which the previous pass re-captured at), and then to `c0570ea60` (0.19.7 plus #136). That move is not packaging: it adds `src/renderer/src/features/chat/clear-search.ts` and rewrites the search field in `src/renderer/src/features/chat/components/chat-sidebar.tsx` (+51/-8), so `srcTree` moved for the first time in any of these rebases, and `scripts/` moved with it (`scripts/clear-search.test.mjs`). A stamp whose tree has moved is exactly the case the earlier passes answered by re-capturing; this one answered it with two facts about the frames. The first is the shape of the change: it paints a clear control INSIDE the field and only while the query is non-empty (the `{query && ...}` guard around the button in `chat-sidebar.tsx`), plus a `pr-9` on the input that reserves the control's column and a `my-2` moved from the input onto a `relative` wrapper around it, which reproduces the same box - so with an empty query the field renders the same placeholder, the same border and the same box as it did before. The second is the measurement that closes it: `clear-search/before-rest` and `clear-search/after-rest` are BYTE-IDENTICAL in both themes, the same empty-query sidebar painted once on the pre-change tree and once on the post-change tree, so nothing in that state depends on #136 at all. Every frame in this tree of that state is therefore unchanged, and the only frames whose state differs are the non-empty-query ones, all of them in `clear-search` itself, which were taken on the changed tree by #136. The sets that carry the field besides `clear-search` were looked at rather than assumed to be empty: `chat-title` and `sidebar-new-chat` draw the empty placeholder with no clear control in all 38 of their frames across both themes, `model-picker-feedback` shows the same empty field behind its scrim, and `mentioned-files-app` is cropped to the canvas panel's own measured rect and carries no sidebar at all; no other set in the tree is about that field - `clear-search`'s own README and readbacks are the only evidence in the tree that names it. Nothing else in the tree was a different source for these pixels either, and that is measurable in the same way: 0 `.webp` differ between the head the previous pass ran at (`98b827108`, orphaned by the force-push that carried this re-stamp) and this head.

THE SYNC MERGE, and what it does and does not claim about the frames. `main` moved three times more - to `6f9bc2d04` (#140: the desktop toolchain, Electron 44 and TypeScript 7), to `4ffc3f2b5` (#139: the New chat row aligned with All chats, without the pill) and to `ad09ec6b4` (the 0.20.1 release) - and this branch was merged up onto it rather than replayed onto it, because a rebase would rewrite all twenty-two commits and orphan every citation this manifest carries while changing no pixel a reader can see. Two paths conflicted: `package.json` (resolved the same way as before - `main`'s `version` line, now 0.20.1, with the UNION of the two sides' `test:desktop` lists, which now carry all three of the test files the sides added, this branch's `mentioned-files.test.mjs` and `main`'s `new-chat-row.test.mjs` and `new-chat-row-evidence.test.mjs`) and this manifest's stamp block, where two re-stamps had to be reconciled; `src/main/index.ts` was auto-merged, both sides' hunks kept. No frame was re-taken for the merge, and the two upstream changes are treated differently for a reason. #140 moves the toolchain (`package.json`, `electron.vite.config.js`, the `tsconfig`s, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, three `scripts/` files, five `src/main/` modules and one renderer component) and not the canvas, the mentioned-files producer or the sidebar, and `main` itself did not re-sweep for it: it re-stamped its trees and committed the toolchain set's own packaged frame beside the swept ones, which is the same position this branch takes for the frames it contributed. #139 does move the sidebar's New chat row, and the three sets that photograph the sidebar (`chat-title`, `sidebar-new-chat` and `model-picker-feedback`'s scrimmed background) predate it: they are pictures of the sidebar as it stood at the heads their `capturedAtHead` fields name, this manifest makes no claim that they show the post-#139 row, and `main` carries that change's own before/after evidence beside them in the `new-chat-row` set - which is why the merge adds that set rather than re-driving those older frames. unchangedControl.why: The honesty check for this pass, and the reason a moved frame is legible as one: a surface this rebase does not paint differently was re-captured through the same command, on the same host, in the same session as the nine it does. All twelve came back BYTE-IDENTICAL, so the encoder and the renderer are deterministic here at this load. The class the moved frames belong to was measured the same way in the previous pass, which ran `audio-viewer` twice: its `neon` frame - which moved in the first run of BOTH passes - came back exactly the committed bytes in that second run. Neither control separates the widget from the encoder for `pdf-viewer/localOperatorDark`, whose difference is the platform PDF plugin not painting at all and which reproduced byte-for-byte instead (see `recaptureNote`).

previousPartialCapture.recaptureNote: Re-captured in place, at the rebased head, and the result is one-sided: 101 of the 108 frames came back BYTE-IDENTICAL to the committed bytes, and all 48 of the four Files surfaces plus all 12 control frames are among them. The 7 that moved are media-viewer frames - pdf 1 (`localOperatorDark`), image 2 (`synth`, `radient`), audio 2 (`neon`, `radient`), video 2 (`synth`, `radient`) - and six of the seven moved only at the lossy encoder's own quantisation scale: at an 8% tolerance (20/255) ZERO pixels differ, and the worst RMSE is 0.00054 (`video-viewer/radient`, 4,342 px of 1,152,000). That class is established rather than assumed: the same command on the same tree was run twice in the previous pass, and `audio-viewer/neon` - which moved in both passes' first runs - came back EXACTLY the committed bytes in one of them, so the movement is the widget repaint and the encoder and a frame that has moved is not read as a change unless it survives a second run. The seventh, `pdf-viewer/localOperatorDark`, is a reproducible platform paint failure and not that class: this session's private headless Chrome never painted the PDF guest document - a probe at 640,200 reads the platform field `srgb(40,40,40)` where the committed frame reads the white page - with a byte-for-byte identical difference (204,364 px, 163,673 of them above 8%) in both passes. The viewer's own source (`pdf-preview.tsx`, `canvas-file-viewer.tsx`, the story) is untouched by `main`'s move, and this branch's canvas hunks in `chat-page.tsx` and `chat-content.tsx` - the one host surface the rebase had to carry - survive line-for-line, so the committed frame is the one that depicts the surface under review; it is retained and NO byte-identity claim is made for it. The 7 frames whose committed bytes are retained are the same picture the re-capture measured.
